source.title: LAION-5B: An open large-scale dataset for training next generation image-text models
source.authors: Christoph Schuhmann; R. Beaumont; R. Vencu; Cade Gordon; Ross Wightman; Mehdi Cherti; Theo Coombes; Aarush Katta; Clayton Mullis; Mitchell Wortsman; P. Schramowski; Srivatsa Kundurthy; K. Crowson; Ludwig Schmidt; R. Kaczmarczyk; J. Jitsev

record.file_problem: None; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-related downstream performance in image-text models, extending the question beyond language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports image-text model accuracy across compute, dataset sizes, and downstream benchmarks. Rows capture its direct scaling sweep (Table 6), the compute-accuracy trend (Figure 4), and its 2B-versus-400M subset comparisons (Table 2). Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: A dataset paper whose CLIP reproduction runs report zero-shot accuracy against compute and dataset size in image-text models (Fig. 4, Table 6, Table 2). This bears on V6 (downstream performance rises with scale) in a new setting. Scaling is a side validation of the dataset, not the paper's main aim, and no loss is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that larger model, data and compute scale improve CLIP zero-shot transfer, with the gain from larger data appearing only with sufficient training compute. The Fig. 4 caption says accuracy increases 'following scale power law'. The main text only says accuracy improves with compute on a log-log plot and leaves possible saturation to future work. They report no exponents and make no predictive claim.
record.recipe_differences: Tests image-text contrastive models and downstream zero-shot accuracy as a function of compute and dataset scale; it does not measure language-model held-out cross-entropy or reproduce the original language-model scaling procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The larger-data benefit in the ViT-B/32 sweep varies with samples seen: LAION-2B-en is below LAION-400M at 3B and 13B samples, but above it at 34B samples (R01–R03).
record.problems: The reported scaling evidence is for downstream vision-language accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss. Figure 4 provides log-log fits but no fit exponents or point values in the text; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The table sweeps cover a limited set of architectures, datasets, and compute levels.
record.rows_left_out: Other downstream benchmark comparisons and retrieval metrics in Tables 2, 7, 8, and 9 are not extracted; the rows prioritize the direct compute sweep, the compute-accuracy figures, and the explicit 2B-versus-400M zero-shot comparisons. The paper's GLIDE and Stable Diffusion examples do not report scaling outcomes.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out loss is measured.
No fit is used to predict larger runs.
There is no comparison of shape at a fixed parameter count.
Only accuracy is measured, not loss. The power-law loss form in image-text or other modalities, repeated data and fine-tuning laws are not tested.
No fitted exponent is reported, nothing is extrapolated to held-out larger runs, and downstream performance is not predicted from pretraining loss. Saturation is explicitly left to future work.
Fitting choices and curvature are not examined.

missing.what: Per-dataset VTAB+ results where LAION-2B underperforms LAION-400M for B/32 on specialized or structured tasks (e.g. Retino 19.1 vs 24.2, PCAM 50.7 vs 55.9, KITTI 17.6 vs 28.8). Scale does not improve every downstream task.
missing.locator: Table 7; Appendix E.3 'Effect of data scale'

missing.what: Few-shot linear-probe accuracy increasing with data (B/32 2B > 400M) and with model size on ImageNet and six other datasets.
Zero-shot retrieval R@k for B/32 LAION-2B vs LAION-400M (e.g. MSCOCO image→text R@1 56.4 vs 53.5).

record.verdict_notes: This is a dataset paper, so the scaling evidence is a secondary validation. No fit parameters or uncertainties are given. Table 2's 2B-vs-400M rows are confounded with samples seen; Table 6 is the clean data-size comparison. V5 is not linked because the study measures accuracy, not loss.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effect of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

Only image-text CLIP-style models and zero-shot accuracy scaling are tested; no image/video generative-model scaling sweep, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning scaling law, or held-out loss law is measured.
Downstream zero-shot classification accuracy is measured against scale; predictability from pretraining loss and other downstream outcome types are not tested.
The paper does not compare fitting choices or exponents, or test curvature away from a single power law.

relationships.condition: CLIP ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 on LAION subsets, zero-shot ImageNet-1k and VTAB+, with more samples seen or larger combined scale
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with samples seen in every sweep (R05, R07, R08, R10, R11, R15, R17). Fig. 4 shows a log-log linear trend with compute (R18, R19). Larger data plus compute improves Table 2 benchmarks (R20–R31, confounded).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased with samples seen in every sweep and followed a linear trend on logarithmic compute axes, while jointly increasing data and compute improved benchmark performance.

source_check.reason: Table 6 shows accuracy increasing with samples seen; Figure 4 shows increasing accuracy with compute and log-log linear fits. Table 2 supports improvements with combined scale, without isolating dataset size.

relationships.condition: Larger dataset (2B vs 400M) at a fixed, lower samples-seen budget
relationships.reason: At 3B and 13B samples, LAION-2B gives lower or equal ImageNet accuracy for B/32 (R02, R03) and a negligible gain for L/14 (R12). The gain appears only at 34B (R01, R13).
relationships.display_finding: At 3B and 13B samples seen, LAION-2B yields lower or equal B/32 accuracy and negligible L/14 gains over 400M data, with improvements appearing only at 34B samples.

source_check.reason: Table 6 shows lower B/32 accuracy at 3B and 13B samples and only a 0.14-point L/14 improvement at 13B, versus larger gains at 34B. These mixed results qualify the benefit of dataset scale by training compute.
